summary: Allow artifactless GitHub Releases for generic repositories

delivery.outcome: Goal creates and repairs the configured GitHub Release for a generic repository without requiring package artifacts, while package fallback remains artifact-bound
nonGoals: No weakening of artifact requirements for Python or other registry-package fallback
No moving, replacing or deleting an existing tag or Release
No automatic publication of Goal itself in this application ticket
No raw GitHub Release command outside governed Goal delivery

architecture.decision: Keep registry fallback artifact-strict, let the create-on-tag path explicitly allow an assetless release only for a detected generic project, and recover an existing annotated exact-HEAD tag after a previously incomplete direct-main run
architecture.rollback: Revert the unmerged ticket branch; new-project keeps its valid immutable tag and records the still-missing Release until a later Goal repair

validation.evidence: Generic create-on-tag creates an assetless Release; registry fallback still rejects missing dist files
A clean direct-main retry reuses only an annotated local tag peeled to exact HEAD and fails closed otherwise

commands: ruff check goal/publish/github_fallback.py goal/push/core.py goal/push/stages/tag.py tests/test_github_fallback.py tests/test_delivery_integrity.py
validation.evidence: Focused, full, governance, static and container contracts pass without dependency changes
The corrected Goal merge repairs new-project v0.16.0 Release from its existing exact annotated tag
